method: Opened official sources through web research. No provider consoles, account data or cloud APIs accessed.
source_scope: Sources support concepts and attributed vendor examples. All fixture schemas, rates, identifiers and exercises are original instructional choices, not provider API emulations.

sources.supports: Five essential characteristics, three service models and four deployment models.
Official full definition and scope; NIST publication states it is not subject to copyright.
Provider infrastructure versus customer-controlled security responsibilities, varying by service.
Illustrative responsibility split and retained data, identity and configuration duties.
Google Cloud parent-child organization, folder and project hierarchy and inheritance.
Azure role-assignment scopes and why narrower resource scope limits affected resources.
AWS security-group purpose and service-specific stateful behavior, not reproduced by the local gates.
Object, file and block storage interface examples.
S3 as an object-storage service, with access and lifecycle choices.
Dynamic scaling policies, targets and bounds; local formula is an original simplified model.
Availability Zone isolation and architecture-dependent resilience; no probability or SLA claim.
Separate RTO and RPO definitions and their distinction from observations.
Business/dependency-based recovery targets and the need to verify recovery methods.
Budget information and notification delay; thresholds are not instant hard caps.
Previewing change sets before execution does not guarantee successful update.
